status_summary: A Hanford amendment to the Tri-Party Agreement and consent decree finalized on 2025-01-10, before the period, provides for grouting low-activity waste from 22 tanks for offsite disposal, and trade press reported that DOE announced on 2025-05-01 a completed 2,000-gallon demonstration shipment of treated tank waste to commercial sites in Texas and Utah. GAO reported in May 2026 that a solicitation for grouting that waste was issued in December 2025 and that DOE had not yet chosen between an onsite grout facility and shipping liquid waste offsite. Congress enacted 8.562 billion dollars for Environmental Management in FY2026 (Public Law 119-74, signed 2026-01-23), 470 million above the request, per CRS. A DOE briefing dated 2026-04-29 shows an FY2027 request of about 8.176 billion dollars, a 5 percent cut, with Hanford down 12 percent, and sets no accelerated completion dates; trade press reported on 2026-04-23 that the Energy Secretary told senators DOE does not expect to seek revisions to the Tri-Party Agreement or consent decree.

timeline.event: Washington Department of Ecology announced the Hanford holistic agreement finalized (before the period): revised Tri-Party Agreement milestones and an amended consent decree approved by a federal district court, providing for retrieval of waste from 22 tanks in the 200 West Area by 2040 with the low-activity portion grouted for offsite disposal, and a DOE decision on a grouting location due by the end of 2025.

DOE announced it had completed a 2,000-gallon demonstration under the Test Bed Initiative, shipping treated low-activity Hanford tank waste to commercial facilities in Texas and Utah for grouting and disposal (announcement date as reported by trade press).

DOE's Hanford tank contractor issued a solicitation for grouting low-activity waste from the 22 tanks, covering either a new onsite grout facility or shipment of liquid waste to existing facilities (month-only date); as of April 2026 proposals were under evaluation, per GAO.

FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations enacted as Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938); per CRS, Environmental Management received 8.562 billion dollars, 470 million above the request and 80 million above FY2025.
The FY2027 budget request was released; trade press reported 8.2 billion dollars sought for Environmental Management, 386 million below FY2026.

DOE budget briefing to site advisory board chairs shows the FY2027 Environmental Management request at 8,176,391 thousand dollars versus 8,562,371 thousand enacted for FY2026 (minus 5 percent), with the Hanford total down 12 percent (slide 5); it does not mention an accelerated completion schedule, grouting, commercial disposal or the Deputy Secretary.

title: Accelerate Environmental Management cleanup and revisit the Hanford framework
uncertainties: Whether DOE applied the high-level waste interpretation more broadly in 2025 and 2026 was not confirmed in primary documents. The demonstration shipment, the FY2027 request release date and the Energy Secretary's 2026-04-23 statement rest on Exchange Monitor reports that are paywalled beyond their opening paragraphs; no DOE primary page on the shipment was reachable. The Energy Secretary's Senate testimony (hearings the article places on the two days before 2026-04-23) is described in the summary but not listed as a timeline event because its exact dates are inferred. The shipment was a demonstration under a program begun earlier. The Ecology release states a grouting-location decision was due by the end of 2025; GAO's May 2026 report (read on its summary page only) says the choice between onsite and offsite grouting was still under evaluation as of April 2026. The CRS report was read through 100,000 of 115,543 characters. The DOE briefing text has no clear slide boundaries, so slide numbers are inferred. No DOE document setting a 2035 or 2060 completion target or a Deputy Secretary reporting line was found.
